verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere's first-party docs show it can act as a coding-agent backend: an OpenAI-compatible endpoint accepts standard clients via `base_url`, a one-command integration points a tool at a model, and the docs reference opencode's `--cloud` flag for using the hosted model. The evidence is thin, however: it names only one agent and has no step-by-step coding-agent setup or hands-on confirmation, so coverage is partial rather than complete. Missing for 10: documented list or setup guides for supported coding agents beyond the single opencode flag reference, detail on agentic features (tool-calling/streaming) through the endpoint for coding workloads, and independent or hands-on corroboration of a coding agent running against it.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can connect a coding agent to this product as a working backend

citations.quote: The endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, so the official OpenAI clients work by pointing `base_url` at it.
One command points a tool at a model and starts it. There is nothing to configure by hand
`--cloud` is an `opencode` flag: it asks for the hosted model rather than one on this machine.
you can use models too large for a laptop while keeping the same tools.
